section: Soil, noise, thermal, marine and radioactive pollution - sources, effects and control
subsections: Noise pollution - unit, Noise Rules 2000 zone limits, silence zones, tolerance, control devices

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the weighting represented by dB(A) in noise measurement?
o: Weighting according to the sensitivity of human hearing
Weighting according to the speed of sound in air
Weighting according to the intensity of ultraviolet radiation
accepted.x: dB(A) is an A-weighted decibel scale that approximates the sensitivity of human hearing at different frequencies.
accepted.tq: Test the exact meaning of a technical suffix rather than merely recalling the unit.
accepted.sec: Noise pollution - unit, Noise Rules 2000 zone limits, silence zones, tolerance, control devices

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding noise exposure:
1. Every rise of about 10 dB roughly doubles the perceived loudness.
2. Exposure above 85 dB can cause permanent hearing loss.
3. Noise around 80 dB is generally treated as hazardous.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: a 10 dB rise roughly doubles loudness, exposure above 85 dB may cause permanent hearing loss, and around 80 dB is regarded as hazardous noise.
accepted.tq: Combine threshold values and identify the option containing all supported statements.
accepted.sec: Noise pollution - unit, Noise Rules 2000 zone limits, silence zones, tolerance, control devices

accepted.s: The Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000 were framed under which enactment?
o: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
accepted.x: The Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000 were framed under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
accepted.tq: Use the parent-law trap by distinguishing closely related environmental statutes.
accepted.sec: Noise pollution - unit, Noise Rules 2000 zone limits, silence zones, tolerance, control devices

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Zone)
a. Industrial
b. Commercial
c. Residential
d. Silence zone

List-II (Day limit in dB(A))
i. 50
ii. 65
iii. 55
iv. 75

Codes:
accepted.x: The prescribed daytime limits are 75 dB(A) for industrial areas, 65 for commercial areas, 55 for residential areas and 50 for silence zones.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair and match the zone limits without confusing day and night values.
accepted.sec: Noise pollution - unit, Noise Rules 2000 zone limits, silence zones, tolerance, control devices

accepted.s:
With reference to the noise limits prescribed for different zones in India, consider the following statements:
1. The night-time limit for a residential area is 45 dB(A).
2. The daytime limit for a commercial area is 65 dB(A).
3. The night-time limit for an industrial area is lower than that for a silence zone.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Residential night and commercial day limits are 45 and 65 dB(A), respectively. Statement 3 is false because the industrial night limit is 70 dB(A), whereas the silence-zone night limit is 40 dB(A).
accepted.tq: Compare rows and columns carefully; the false statement reverses the relative limits of two zones.
accepted.sec: Noise pollution - unit, Noise Rules 2000 zone limits, silence zones, tolerance, control devices

accepted.s: The day period for applying the prescribed ambient noise standards is generally taken as:
accepted.x: For the noise standards, day is generally reckoned from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m.; the remaining period is treated as night.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the fixed time boundary from nearby but incorrect hour ranges.
accepted.sec: Noise pollution - unit, Noise Rules 2000 zone limits, silence zones, tolerance, control devices

accepted.s: A silence zone under the Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000 extends at least how far around hospitals, educational institutions and courts?
accepted.x: A silence zone is an area extending at least 100 metres around hospitals, educational institutions and courts.
accepted.tq: Test a protected-area distance using four close numerical alternatives.
accepted.sec: Noise pollution - unit, Noise Rules 2000 zone limits, silence zones, tolerance, control devices

accepted.s: Firecrackers are prohibited during which period under the specified noise-control provisions?
accepted.x: The specified prohibition period for fireworks is from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact start and end times; both boundaries are potential traps.
accepted.sec: Noise pollution - unit, Noise Rules 2000 zone limits, silence zones, tolerance, control devices

accepted.s: The Central Pollution Control Board restricts firecrackers producing noise above which level when measured at four metres from the point of bursting?
accepted.x: CPCB restricts firecrackers exceeding 125 dB when measured at a distance of four metres from the point of bursting.
accepted.tq: Link the numerical limit with its prescribed measurement distance.
accepted.sec: Noise pollution - unit, Noise Rules 2000 zone limits, silence zones, tolerance, control devices

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding noise monitoring in India is correct?
o: NANMN monitors only industrial zones in two metropolitan cities.
NANMN has 100 stations in all State capitals.
NANMN has 25 stations confined to Andhra Pradesh.
NANMN has 70 stations in seven metropolitan cities.
accepted.x: The CPCB Real Time National Ambient Noise Monitoring Network has 70 stations in seven metros: Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru, Lucknow and Hyderabad.
accepted.tq: Use the network’s count-and-coverage combination to reject swapped figures and locations.
accepted.sec: Noise pollution - unit, Noise Rules 2000 zone limits, silence zones, tolerance, control devices

accepted.s: Which of the following cities is NOT included among the seven metropolitan cities covered by the CPCB's Real Time National Ambient Noise Monitoring Network?
accepted.x: The seven listed cities are Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru, Lucknow and Hyderabad. Ahmedabad is not included in this specified network list.
accepted.tq: Find the omitted location from a fixed membership list.
accepted.sec: Noise pollution - unit, Noise Rules 2000 zone limits, silence zones, tolerance, control devices

accepted.s: According to the stated assessment, what proportion of monitored sites in Delhi breach the prescribed noise limits?
accepted.x: The reported assessment places the proportion of Delhi sites breaching the limits between 65 and 85 percent.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct range rather than a single rounded percentage.
accepted.sec: Noise pollution - unit, Noise Rules 2000 zone limits, silence zones, tolerance, control devices

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to common sound levels?
accepted.x: A whisper is approximately 30 dB. Conversation is about 60 dB, heavy traffic about 90 dB and a jet take-off about 140 dB.
accepted.tq: Use magnitude comparison to detect reversed or exaggerated sound-level pairings.
accepted.sec: Noise pollution - unit, Noise Rules 2000 zone limits, silence zones, tolerance, control devices

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): Prolonged exposure to high noise levels can increase blood pressure and disturb sleep.
Reason (R): Noise exposure may raise cortisol levels in the body.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both statements are true, and the stress response involving increased cortisol helps explain the effects of prolonged noise exposure on blood pressure and sleep.
accepted.tq: Check whether the physiological mechanism directly explains the stated health effects.
accepted.sec: Noise pollution - unit, Noise Rules 2000 zone limits, silence zones, tolerance, control devices

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as an effect of prolonged noise exposure?
accepted.x: Prolonged noise exposure may constrict blood vessels, cause digestive spasms and impair night vision. It does not improve night vision.
accepted.tq: Locate the single reversed health effect in an otherwise related list.
accepted.sec: Noise pollution - unit, Noise Rules 2000 zone limits, silence zones, tolerance, control devices

accepted.s:
A municipal authority plans to reduce traffic noise along a highway near a school. Which combination is most consistent with recognised noise-control measures?
1. Installing sound barriers
2. Developing green belts along the highway
3. Imposing suitable loudspeaker restrictions
4. Improving traffic management

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Sound barriers, green belts, loudspeaker curbs and traffic management are all recognised measures for controlling noise pollution. Zoning and silencers or mufflers are additional measures.
accepted.tq: Apply the control-measure list to a realistic administrative situation.
accepted.sec: Noise pollution - unit, Noise Rules 2000 zone limits, silence zones, tolerance, control devices

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Constitutional provision)
a. Article 21
b. Article 48A
c. Article 51A(g)

d. Sustainable Development Goal 6

List-II (Environmental association)
i. Protection and improvement of the environment as a Directive Principle
ii. Protection of life and personal liberty
 iii. Fundamental duty to protect and improve the natural environment
iv. Clean water and sanitation

Codes:
accepted.x: Article 21 concerns life and personal liberty; Article 48A concerns environmental protection; Article 51A(g) is the environmental fundamental duty; SDG 6 concerns clean water and sanitation.
accepted.tq: Start with the familiar constitutional article and complete the environmental association pairs.
accepted.sec: Pollution type → major source

accepted.s: Which one of the following pollution types is correctly associated with its major primary source and constitutional or developmental linkage?
o: Soil pollution — chemical fertilisers and pesticides — Article 48A and SDGs 2 and 15
Radioactive pollution — sewage discharge — Article 48A and SDG 11
Thermal pollution — vehicle exhaust — Article 21 and SDG 13
Marine pollution — uranium mining — Article 51A(g) and SDG 6
accepted.x: Soil pollution is primarily associated with chemical fertilisers and pesticides, and its listed linkages are Article 48A and SDGs 2 and 15. The other options mismatch both sources and linkages.
accepted.tq: Compare source, constitutional provision and SDG together rather than relying on one column.
accepted.sec: Pollution type → major source

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding thermal, marine and radioactive pollution are correct?
1. Thermal pollution is associated with cooling water released from thermal and nuclear power plants.
2. Marine pollution may result from oil spills, plastics, sewage and river-borne pollutants.
3. Radioactive pollution may arise from nuclear plants, nuclear tests, mining and medical waste.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly identify the principal sources listed for thermal, marine and radioactive pollution.
accepted.tq: Group related source statements and select the comprehensive combination when every item fits.
accepted.sec: Pollution type → major source

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Noise pollution — construction, traffic and loudspeakers
Thermal pollution — cooling water from thermal and nuclear power plants
Marine pollution — exclusively radioactive waste from hospitals
Air pollution — industrial emissions and vehicles
accepted.x: Marine pollution has several major sources, including land runoff, plastics, oil and sewage; it is not exclusively caused by radioactive hospital waste.
accepted.tq: Reject the option using the extreme word ‘exclusively’ and compare it with the complete source range.
accepted.sec: Pollution type → major source

accepted.s: Which pollution type is primarily associated with chemical fertilisers and pesticides?
accepted.x: Chemical fertilisers and pesticides are identified as the major primary sources of soil pollution.
accepted.tq: Test a single source-to-pollution association while avoiding the broader source list.
